article.citation: Paller, V. G. V., Corpuz, M. N. C., & Bandal, M. Z. Jr. (2017). Freshwater fish assemblages and water quality parameters in Seven Lakes of San Pablo, Laguna, Philippines. Asian Journal of Biodiversity, 8(1), 1-22. https://doi.org/10.7828/ajob.v8i1.995
publisherPageFacts: The publisher record identifies the 2017 article and reports an aggregate survey of 5,166 fish samples and ten taxa across the Seven Lakes of San Pablo.
The article describes monthly sampling during February 2013-January 2014 and April 2014-March 2015.
The extracted article text identifies Appendix Table 2 as the per-lake freshwater-fish distribution table, but does not expose its cells.
article.access: The official article page and PDF text were reviewed through web extraction on 2026-11-05. No local copy was retained. A direct shell request for the PDF returned a Cloudflare JavaScript/cookie challenge; it was not bypassed.

publisherPolicy.citation: Asian Journal of Biodiversity. (2026). Editorial Policy, Vol. 17 No. 1, January 2026.
statementsReviewed: The policy describes AJOB as open access and permits readers to read, download, copy, distribute, print, search, or link to full-text articles without prior authorization.
The policy states that authors transfer copyright to AJOB.
limits: No Creative Commons license is identified in the reviewed policy text.
The policy does not expressly discuss structured extraction, derivative occurrence databases, or public-app display.
The policy gives no explicit effective-date or retrospective-application statement for the 2017 article.

reuseAssessment.interpretation: The journal-wide policy is positive evidence for copying and distributing full article text, but it is not an explicit item-level license for extracting the table into a structured public species product. Do not interpret free full-text access alone as permission to republish the table or its layout.
reuseAssessment.decision: Keep per-lake species rows in research-only review until the Table 2 cells are available for accurate transcription and the policy's applicability to structured factual display is clear, or an independently eligible source supports the same lake-specific facts.

evidenceLimits: The 2017 paper reports historical survey sampling from 2013 through 2015; it does not establish present-day fish presence or abundance.
The study reports ten taxa in aggregate, but the current review did not transcribe per-lake table cells.

The Bunot carp identity remains conflicted: the 2017 narrative and plate identify Carassius gibelio, while the 2021 secondary review reports Carassius carassius; neither reviewed source supplies a voucher-level resolution.
Museum-index searches returning zero exact waterbody matches do not prove absence or lack of sampling.
nextAction: Continue the CALABARZON freshwater source sweep with an independently accessible, locality-resolved dataset. If revisiting this survey, use a normal publisher-provided PDF route or request clarification from AJOB about structured public factual reuse; do not bypass access controls or infer table cells from the aggregate abstract.
